assumptions.limine.version: 12.9.6. Omarchy names the package without a version (install/omarchy-other.packages:20-22) and the repo holds no PKGBUILD or ISO pin for it. Arch extra/limine was 12.9.6-1 (updated 2026-10-28) when this was read, and v12.9.6 (89a9512c623a4779cc73e3869383876d54264b28, tagged 2026-10-28) is the newest tag before the Omarchy commit (2026-11-01). Omarchy may ship from its own mirror; that was not checked.
assumptions.firmware: x86_64 UEFI, Secure Boot off, no config hash enrolled (ENABLE_ENROLL_LIMINE_CONFIG is commented out: https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-entry-tool/-/blob/1.40.0/install/arch-linux/limine-mkinitcpio-hook/etc/limine-entry-tool.conf#L151), so the editor is enabled (https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/lib/misc.c#L121 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c)). The firmware advertises EFI_OS_INDICATIONS_BOOT_TO_FW_UI, which most do; without it the 'S Firmware Setup' hint is dropped. No shellx64.efi on the ESP, so no 'U UEFI Shell' hint.
assumptions.display: One GOP output. Limine picks the EDID-native mode (the first detailed timing) at 32 bpp when it is at least the current mode; otherwise the firmware's preset mode (https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/drivers/gop.c#L374-L399 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c)). Worked numbers below use 1920x1080 and 2560x1600.
assumptions.install: Default x86_64 install: one kernel (linux-omarchy) built as a UKI, snapper enabled, no Windows or other OS on the ESP, no MKINITCPIO_FALLBACK (only the n1x hardware path sets it: install/hardware/n1x.sh:94).
assumptions.colours: Every colour is a literal from default/limine/limine.conf:5-21 (Tokyo Night). Limine draws in 24-bit RGB; its own SGR palette indices map to term_palette.

quiet.layout: With 'timeout: 1' and 'quiet: yes', Limine draws nothing. It never starts its graphical terminal, prints nothing, and does not clear the screen, so whatever the firmware left (usually the OEM BGRT logo, or black) stays up for one second. The cursor is hidden. A key press in that second reveals the menu, but that key is swallowed and the countdown is cancelled, so the revealed menu waits with no timeout. If no key comes, Limine boots entry 2 (linux-omarchy) without touching the screen. The mouse cannot reveal the menu, because the mouse is not initialised in quiet mode.

items.what: quiet: yes switches all screen output off except panics and important warnings
Timeout parsed to milliseconds
default_entry is a 1-based index over visible entries, counting expanded directories. Index 2 is the first kernel under the expanded 'Omarchy' directory

Autoboot runs only if the default entry resolves to a bootable leaf. A directory or an unresolved entry turns quiet off and shows the menu ('Default entry is not valid, booting to menu.' for the unresolved case)
items.expr: if unresolved: quiet=false, print msg; if sub!=NULL: skip_timeout; skip_timeout => quiet=false

items.what: In quiet mode menu_init_term does not call gterm_init, and gterm_init returns early in quiet mode. No framebuffer terminal exists
items.expr: if (!quiet && !gterm_init(...)); gterm_init: if (quiet) { term_notready(); return false; }

items.what: print() writes nothing to the terminal while quiet is set
The screen is not cleared at startup, so the firmware's BGRT logo survives
items.expr: // XXX: Ideally we clear the screen, but that gets rid of the BGRT boot logo

items.what: The UEFI text cursor is disabled at entry
The countdown loop still runs, invisibly: one 1000 ms wait that returns early on input
Mouse is initialised only when not quiet, so only the keyboard can interrupt
Any key during the timeout: skip_timeout = true, then quiet = false, the terminal is initialised and the menu is drawn. The key is not acted on, and no countdown follows
items.expr: goto timeout_aborted -> if (quiet) { quiet=false; menu_init_term(); mouse_init(); goto refresh; }

items.what: The reveal is immediate on the key press (the wait polls input), not at the end of the second

When the timeout ends it goes to autoboot. In quiet mode there is no reset_term, and chainload's fb_init keeps the screen (quiet forces preserve_screen). Limine then LoadImage/StartImage's the UKI. The GOP may be switched to the EDID-native mode first if the firmware was in another mode, and a mode set usually blanks the screen. That depends on the firmware
items.expr: fb_init: if (quiet) preserve_screen = true; chainload -> gBS->StartImage

items.what: firmware_logo is unset (default no), so Limine does not ask the OS to redraw the BGRT logo

grid.layout: With no wallpaper, the whole screen is one flat terminal in term_background 1a1b26, with no margin, no gradient and no frame. Cells use the built-in Toshiba Satellite 8x16 font, one pixel of spacing (9x16 cells), scaled by an integer factor chosen from the resolution. The grid is centred in the framebuffer and the leftover pixels are split equally on each side. The main menu has no box. The framed box (┌─┤title├─┐) appears only in the 'E' editor.

items.what: Built-in font: the Toshiba Satellite 8x16 VGA font (TOSH-SAT.F16), code page 437, 256 glyphs. Glyph n is at gterm.c line 21+n
Glyph bitmap size (no term_font set)
Horizontal spacing between glyphs (term_font_spacing unset)
items.source: https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/lib/gterm.c#L732-L742 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c); https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm_backends/fb.c#L1433-L1436 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80)

items.what: The ninth (spacing) column is blank, except for CP437 0xC0-0xDF (box drawing), where it repeats column 8. So ─ └ ├ join across cells and ► does not
Font scale, since term_font_scale is unset
Cell size on screen
Columns and rows
items.value: cols = floor(W / cellW); rows = floor(H / cellH)

items.what: The grid is centred: half the leftover pixels go before it (rounded down)
1920x1080: scale 1, cell 9x16
2560x1600: scale 2, cell 18x32
3840x2160: scale 2 (4x needs 5120x2880), cell 18x32
If the grid is under 40x16, Limine falls back to the firmware text console
term_margin and term_margin_gradient default to 0 when there is no wallpaper. Omarchy sets neither and has no wallpaper
Whole-screen fill. term_background is TTRRGGBB; '1a1b26' has TT=00, which is opaque. With no wallpaper there is no canvas, and a full refresh paints every framebuffer pixel default_bg
items.expr: default_bg = strtoui("1a1b26") = 0x001a1b26; plot_char_*_uncanvas; full_refresh fills default_bg
items.source: default/limine/limine.conf:11; https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/lib/gterm.c#L592-L595 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c); https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/lib/gterm.c#L506-L509 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c); https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm_backends/fb.c#L1135-L1160 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80)

items.what: 'backdrop: 1a1b26' has no effect. It is read only for a wallpaper with wallpaper_style centered, and Omarchy sets no wallpaper
Resolution: interface_resolution is unset, so Limine tries the EDID-native mode at 32 bpp, then the firmware preset mode, then 1024x768/800x600/640x480

The text cursor is off while the menu draws. With a mouse, after it moves by more than one cell, a 16x16 arrow sprite (black outline, white fill, scaled by the font scale, hotspot top-left) follows the pointer

menu.layout: Rows from the top, 0-based. Row 0 is blank. Row 1 holds the branding, centred. Row 3 holds the primary help, centred. Row 5 holds the secondary help, centred. The tree is vertically centred, never higher than row 8, and is one left-aligned block whose left edge is chosen to centre the widest line. Row rows-2 holds the selected entry's first 'comment:' in cyan, centred. ↑↑↑ (row 7) and ↓↓↓ (row rows-4) appear only when the list scrolls. Everything uses term_foreground c0caf5 on 1a1b26 unless stated. Every row is redrawn from scratch on each key ('\e[2J\e[H').

items.what: Each refresh clears the screen, homes the cursor and moves to row 1
header_offset = 2 (branding present) + 2 (secondary help present: editor enabled or firmware setup or shell)
Branding string, verbatim. No Limine version and no Secure Boot suffix, because it is custom
Row 1, horizontally centred by display width. If it is wider than cols-2, it is cut to cols-5 characters plus '...' at column 1
Branding colour, set as a 24-bit SGR
Primary help when the selection is a bootable entry and the editor is enabled. Keys are in the help colour, labels in the default foreground, with four spaces between pairs
items.value: ARROWS Select    ENTER Boot    E Edit

items.what: Primary help when the selection is a directory: 'Collapse' if expanded, 'Expand' if collapsed
items.value: ARROWS Select    ENTER Collapse | ARROWS Select    ENTER Expand

items.what: Secondary help, row 5, centred. Shown pairs: S if the firmware supports boot-to-firmware-UI, U if shellx64.efi is on the ESP, B if the editor is enabled. Labels shorten to Setup/Shell/Blank if the line would be wider than cols
items.value: S Firmware Setup    B Blank Entry

items.what: Key glyphs ARROWS/ENTER/E/S/B colour. Labels follow '\e[0m', so they are term_foreground
interface_help_hidden is unset, so both help rows show
Visible tree rows (scroll window)
First tree row: the tree is centred vertically, but never above row 8
Every tree line starts after the same run of spaces, chosen from the widest line (max_tree_len counts decorations plus ' name ')
Top-level entry prefix: '[-]' expanded directory, '[+]' collapsed directory, three spaces for a leaf

Nested entry prefix: for each ancestor level above the parent, ' │' if that ancestor has a later sibling, else two spaces. Then ' └' for the last sibling or ' ├' otherwise. Then '[-]'/'[+]' for a directory or '──►' for a leaf
The name is printed as ' ' + name + ' '. A name too wide for the row is cut and ends in '...'

Selection highlight: reverse video starts after the prefix, so it covers ' name ' (one space each side) and not the tree glyphs. In reverse video the background is term_foreground and the glyphs are term_background
items.expr: \e[7m swaps text_fg (default_fg c0caf5) and text_bg (default flag) -> bg=c0caf5, fg_default -> default_bg 1a1b26
items.source: https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine/blob/v12.9.6/common/menu.c#L1428-L1431 (limine v12.9.6, 89a9512c); https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm.c#L361-L367 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80); https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm_backends/fb.c#L563-L571 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80); https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm_backends/fb.c#L638-L642 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80)

items.what: Tree glyphs, brackets and names of unselected entries
items.source: default/limine/limine.conf:11,19; https://github.com/Mintsuki/Flanterm/blob/3e311fe2ce4f663273c22d1a229745bc53afa930/src/flanterm_backends/fb.c#L1388-L1392 (Flanterm 3e311fe2, pinned by limine v12.9.6 bootstrap:77-80)

items.what: Tree glyphs are UTF-8 mapped to CP437: ─ 0xC4, ├ 0xC3, └ 0xC0, │ 0xB3, ► 0x10, ↑ 0x18, ↓ 0x19
Scroll markers, centred: '↑↑↑' at row 3+header_offset (7) when entries are hidden above, '↓↓↓' at row rows-4 when hidden below
The selected entry's first 'comment:' value, in cyan (SGR 36 = term_palette[6]), centred at row rows-2 (rows-3 while a countdown runs). Cut with '...' if too wide
Countdown string. It has no 'press any key' text. It is never visible with Omarchy's config: quiet hides it, and revealing the menu cancels it
items.expr: "\e[2K%sBooting automatically in %s%s%s...\e[0m" (help colour, bright help colour for N); x = (cols - (28+len(N)))/2, row rows-2

items.what: Countdown text and digit. Omarchy sets interface_help_color_bright to the same green

Up/Down move and wrap. Home/End jump. Enter, Space or Right boots a leaf or toggles a directory. 1-9 boots that visible index at once. E opens the editor. B opens a blank entry. S reboots to firmware setup. Left is ignored. The mouse moves the selection, a click boots, and the wheel scrolls

Choosing an entry from the revealed menu clears to 1a1b26 (reset_term), then chainload's fb_init clears the framebuffer to 0x000000 on x86 (fb_flush_reliable is true there, so preserve_screen is false). Then the UKI starts

entries.layout:
limine-entry-tool writes Omarchy's OS directory, '/+Omarchy'. The '+' makes it expanded at boot. Its children follow BOOT_ORDER: linux-omarchy first, Snapshots last. limine-snapper-sync owns '//Snapshots', which is collapsed. Inside it, one collapsed directory per snapshot, newest first, each holding the kernel entries saved with it. Default visible tree:
[-] Omarchy
 ├──► linux-omarchy      <- default_entry 2, selected
 └[+] Snapshots
With Snapshots expanded (five snapshots, upstream default format):
 └[-] Snapshots
   ├[+] ID=5 2026-11-01 18:10:30
   ├[+] ID=4 …
   └[+] ID=1 …
An expanded snapshot holds '──► linux-omarchy'.

items.what: OS directory name, created expanded
Comment shown when 'Omarchy' is selected (the first comment line is the clean name). The second line is 'machine-id=<id> order-priority=50'
Kernel entry name: the kernel's pkgbase. A UKI is written to /EFI/Linux/omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi
First comment of the kernel entry, shown in cyan when selected. The second is 'kernel-id=linux-omarchy'
Children order
No '-fallback' kernel entry by default: MKINITCPIO_FALLBACK is unset. ENABLE_LIMINE_FALLBACK=yes copies Limine itself to /EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI and adds no menu entry

Possible top-level leaf 'EFI fallback' (comment 'Default EFI loader', priority 10, placed after Omarchy). FIND_BOOTLOADERS=yes adds it when limine-install runs while /EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI already exists. Whether a default install reaches that state was not pinned
Snapshots directory inside the OS entry, collapsed
Snapshots comment: 'N snapshots'. It reads 'N / 6 snapshots' only if MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES reaches the tool (see notes)

Snapshot directory name. Upstream default format 0 is 'ID=<n> <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>' (id left-padded to the widest id). Omarchy asks for format 5, the timestamp alone ('2026-11-01 18:10:30'), but see notes on whether it applies
items.expr: snapshotNameFormat: case 5 -> timestamp; default -> "ID=" + id + " " + timestamp

items.what: Newest snapshot first. At most 5 kept by snapper (NUMBER_LIMIT=5), briefly 6
A snapshot's comment is its snapper description. Omarchy's updater creates snapshots described with omarchy-version
Leaf inside each snapshot directory: the kernel entry name saved with that snapshot
Visible indices (default tree, Snapshots collapsed): 1 Omarchy, 2 linux-omarchy, 3 Snapshots (+1 'EFI fallback' if present)

handoff.layout: What the screen shows from Limine's last frame until Plymouth draws. Default (quiet) path: Limine never paints, so the firmware's image stays (BGRT logo or black) unless the GOP mode set blanks it. The UKI's kernel runs with quiet logging and a hidden console cursor, so nothing new prints. Plymouth, from the initramfs, then fills the screen with its 1a1b26 background. Revealed-menu path: a black (#000000) screen from chainload's clear until Plymouth. Limine's 1a1b26 is never left on screen.

items.what: Kernel cmdline that silences the console
items.value: quiet splash loglevel=0 systemd.show_status=false rd.udev.log_level=0 vt.global_cursor_default=0 (+ initramfs_async=0 systemd.tty.term.console=dumb)

items.what: Quiet path: no Limine clear before StartImage
Revealed-menu path: framebuffer cleared to black before StartImage
Plymouth's background: the first colour after the hand-off that Omarchy controls

notes: Version: Limine v12.9.6 differs from older screenshots, including limine-snapper-sync's own (screenshots/2.jpg). In v12 both help rows are centred, primary at row 3 and secondary at row 5. Older versions put 'ARROWS Select / ENTER …' on the left and 'S Firmware Setup / B Blank Entry' on the right. The countdown reads 'Booting automatically in N...' and has no 'press any key to stop' text.

Conflict, not pinned: Omarchy sets SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_CHOICE=5 and MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES=6 in /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-defaults.conf:35-37. limine-snapper-sync 1.32.1 reads only /etc/limine-snapper-sync.conf, /etc/default/limine and (inside a snapshot) /tmp/limine-snapper-sync.conf (https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-snapper-sync/-/blob/1.32.1/src/main/java/org/limine/snapper/processes/ConfigReader.java#L22-41 (limine-snapper-sync 1.32.1, b4c0da2d)). It does not read limine-entry-tool.d drop-ins, unlike limine-entry-tool (https://gitlab.com/Zesko/limine-entry-tool/-/blob/1.40.0/src/main/java/org/limine/entry/tool/processes/ConfigReader.java#L29-31 (limine-entry-tool 1.40.0, 35dab4b7)). Read strictly, snapshot names would be the default 'ID=<n> <timestamp>' with the comment 'N snapshots'. But the comment at omarchy-defaults.conf:30-34 quotes a snapper-sync warning about MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES=5, which implies the setting does reach it on real systems, perhaps through a packaged build that differs from the AUR source. For the demo, the timestamp-only form ('2026-11-01 18:10:30') matches Omarchy's intent. 'ID=5 2026-11-01 18:10:30' matches the pinned upstream source.

Omarchy's own test fixtures write snapshot names as '<id> │ <timestamp>' (format 2: test/shell.d/omarchy-kernel-test.sh:71, factory-reset-limine-test.sh:60). These are hand-written mocks, not output, and neither the pinned source nor Omarchy's setting produces that format.

The firmware's image during the quiet second is not Limine's to decide. Most laptops show the OEM BGRT logo, others black. A GOP mode switch to the EDID-native mode before the kernel can blank it. The demo should show a plain black or vendor-logo screen for about 1 s, then go straight to Plymouth.
Revealing the menu needs a key press inside that ~1 s window, and the key that reveals it does nothing else. After that the menu never times out.

Exact strings: branding 'Omarchy Bootloader'; 'ARROWS Select    ENTER Boot    E Edit'; 'ARROWS Select    ENTER Expand' / 'ARROWS Select    ENTER Collapse'; 'S Firmware Setup    B Blank Entry' (short form 'S Setup    B Blank' when narrow; 'U UEFI Shell' / 'U Shell' between them if shellx64.efi exists); 'Booting automatically in N...'; editor 'ESC Discard and Exit    F10/CTRL+X Boot'; 'Default entry is not valid, booting to menu.'; '[config file contains no valid entries]'; '[config file not found]'. Gaps between key pairs are four spaces.

Glyph fidelity: a web replica should render the Toshiba Satellite 8x16 bitmaps from gterm.c:21-276 (glyph n at line 21+n) on a 9-pixel advance, repeating column 8 into column 9 for CP437 0xC0-0xDF. A generic monospace font will not join '├──►' the way Limine does.
